changes.after: An assignment can give names to the first and last items and gather whatever is between them.

before: Multiple assignment distributes array elements across names. With first, *middle, last, the outer names take the ends and the starred name gathers the remaining elements into an array.

If no elements remain for the starred name it gets an empty array. Unfilled ordinary positions receive nil. A name such as _ignored signals an unused value by convention; unlike an exact shape pattern, this assignment does not reject a shorter array.

Complete local Ruby example; the app itself does not execute it:
```ruby
first, *middle, last = [10, 20, 30, 40]
puts first
puts middle.inspect
puts last
```

Expected output or behavior: 10
[20, 30]
40. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Put all items between the ends into an array.

Follow the labeled parts of this example.
```ruby
first, *middle, last = [10, 20, 30, 40]
puts first
puts middle.inspect
puts last
```
The output is `10`, then `[20, 30]`, then `40`. Ten and forty go to the ends. Twenty and thirty go into the middle array.
Remove both middle numbers without changing the ends.
